title: Karger survival lower bound for a minimum cut
statement: Let $n \ge 2$ and let $T$ be a surviving trace of $n-2$ steps, indexing states $T_0, T_1, \ldots$ each consisting of a multigraph together with a distinguished cut. Suppose the distinguished cut of the initial state $T_0$ is a minimum cut of its graph, that this initial graph has exactly $n$ vertices, and that for every step index $i < n-2$ the graph of $T_i$ has at least two vertices. Then the product of the uniform one-step survival probabilities of the states $T_0, \ldots, T_{n-3}$ satisfies \[ \frac{2}{n(n-1)} \le \prod_{i=0}^{n-3} p_i, \] where $p_i$ is the number of edges of $T_i$ not crossing its distinguished cut divided by the total edge count of $T_i$.
hypotheses_covered: T is a surviving trace of n-2 steps
the distinguished cut of the initial state is a minimum cut
the initial graph has exactly n vertices
every state before the last has a graph with at least 2 vertices
replaced:
Under the same hypotheses as the product-level bound, the product of the concrete uniform
one-step survival probabilities along the trace is at least $2/(n(n-1))$.
